- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) in recent days, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast slightly to avoid bearish overcorrection.  
- Model consistently underestimates price spikes in the 3rd–5th day of a new trend — adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for such periods.  
- Model overestimates early in 30-day horizon — especially after a sharp spike — apply downward correction of 1–2% for days 1–3.  
- Model shows mean reversion bias — if 30-day forecast is above 70, reduce by 0.5–1.0% for next 5 days; if below 65, increase by 0.5–1.0%.  
- Sentiment + price spike = model lags — forecast should be adjusted 1–2 days ahead of true outcome when sentiment is rising.  
- If sentiment history shows 2+ consecutive 0.00 values, model tends to be flat — introduce slight upward bias (0.2–0.5%) to avoid underestimation.
